factors.name: Size and branching volume
factors.summary: Very high loadings (0.90–0.97) of Token split, Number of empty sequence flows, Control flow complexity, Size and Coefficient of network connectivity show that larger nets in this dataset also have more splits, more parallel places and more arcs per node. Maximum connector degree (0.76, also 0.39 on Factor 2) and Connector Mismatch (0.55, communality only 0.35) join more weakly. Density loads -0.46 here, so larger nets tend to be sparser.

factors.name: Connector degree and density
factors.summary: Average connector degree (0.89) and Density (0.84) load together, with Connector Heterogeneity negative (-0.58). The factor describes compact nets whose connectors carry many arcs and that tend to use one connector type rather than a mix. Density also loads -0.46 on Factor 1, and Heterogeneity has a low communality (0.35).

factors.name: Sequential, separable structure
factors.summary: Sequentiality (0.96) and Separability (0.69) define this factor, which reflects nets with many plain sequence arcs and many articulation points, i.e. chain-like structure. It rests on only two measures, and Sequentiality is a possible Heywood case (communality 1.017), so the factor is fragile.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, overall KMO 0.83). Three varimax factors explain 82% of the variance. A dominant size and branching factor (49%) is followed by a connector-degree/density factor (17%) and a sequentiality/separability factor (16%). Every measure is assigned and no formal cross-loadings are flagged. Maximum connector degree, Density and Coefficient of network connectivity nonetheless show notable secondary loadings.
caveats: Sequentiality has a communality above 1 (possible Heywood case), so the Factor 3 solution may be unstable.
Factor 3 is carried by only two measures and its eigenvalue (1.2) is only just above 1.
Connector Mismatch and Connector Heterogeneity have low communalities (about 0.35) and are poorly explained by the factors.
Connector Heterogeneity, Average connector degree and Density have MSA values only slightly above 0.6.
Connector Heterogeneity is undefined for nets without connectors, and how such cases were handled is not reported.
Number of duplicate tasks was constant and removed, so the analysis says nothing about label duplication.
Varimax forces the factors to be orthogonal, and the results reflect shared variance in this set of 288 nets, not causal relations.
